content.text: I'm running a patched 3.3 install to address this; I can get it into trunk easily if the solution sits well with everyone.

The description here is a little opaque to me, but the label and related ticket makes me think this is the same problem I just ran into with Fedora 3.4 - trying to ingest new objects using file:/// URIs for datastream content, when I provide a checksum type and a checksum I get the "Checksum Mismatch: ExceptionReadingStream" error; however, if I don't specify either or when I only specify a checksum type the objects ingest just fine (and the checksum is calculated correctly).  Here's an example of the fedora log output when it errors, in case it's helpful:
ERROR 2011-12-19 17:26:08.328 [http-8943-8] (FedoraObjectResource) Unexpected error fulfilling REST API request
org.fcrepo.server.errors.ObjectIntegrityException: FOXML IO stream was bad : Checksum Mismatch: ExceptionReadingStream
This issue should have been fixed in 3.5, along with FCREPO-776.
Thanks for the update.  I will test on 3.5 when I get a chance and report back.
This doesn't appear to be working in 3.5.  I've got a test to demonstrate,and am now trying to figure out what I meant about read-only contexts when I posted this issue.  Sigh.

I should have the test and fix for this pushed to master soon.  In the meantime, I think you should be able to work around this by adding a policy that permits API-M if the action is "urn:fedora:names:fedora:2.1:action:id-retrieveFile"; your other policy should still block unallowed file paths.  You might add something about there being a nil client IP to that condition if you want to firm it up more, but that will eventually break.
Sorry this took so long- it ended up being a bear to fix it in FESL. In master at:

Replicates fcrepo-696, with the additional problem that an empty read-only context is insufficient for policy resolution.  I think the solution is to add the ability to attach a context to DatastreamReferencedContent (and arguably to DatastreamManagedContent, which would have the same problem if it enforced a policy regarding the URLs it would fetch).
